Event definition: In the advance after Bluecoat, by nightfall on the 5th the 53rd Division has cleared the east bank of the Orne almost to Grimbosq and on its right the 59th Division, with the brigade and the 56th Infantry Brigade under command, has reached the river further upstream; from the loop of the Orne near Thury-Harcourt the line bends back westwards (p. 408). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. current_activity: Astonia: under the 49th Division, attacks the north plateau of Le Havre from 17:30
notes: Event date: 10 September 1944, from 17:30 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 14; Stacey, p. 332; Wikipedia: the brigade arrived outside Le Havre on 6 September). Event definition: As soon as the last heavy bomber attack ends at 5.30 p.m. on the 10th, I Corps attacks; the 49th Division, with the brigade under command, sets out from the north-east to capture the defences of the north plateau and then to cross the Fontaine valley (Ellis, p. 14; Stacey, p. 332, the same in the plan); Wikipedia: on arrival outside Le Havre on 6 September the brigade came under command of the 49th Division, and the garrison surrendered on 12 September. Event support: three source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Stacey, the Canadian official history, and Wikipedia). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 14: "The 49th Division, with the 34th Tank Brigade under command, set out from the north-east to capture the defences of the north plateau"; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 332: "In the opening phase the 49th Division, with the 34th Tank Brigade"; Wikipedia, 34th Armoured Brigade (page 34th Tank Brigade): "On arrival outside Le Havre on 6 September, the brigade came under command of 49th (West Riding) Infantry Division". Location: Le Havre (PL0169) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Le Havre; the brigade attacked the north plateau from the north-east. Location support: Ellis, Stacey and Wikipedia put the brigade on the north-east side of Le Havre and name no village. Commander: Brig. W. S. Clarke, commander from June 1943 (Wikipedia, 34th Armoured Brigade).

notes: Event date: 20 October 1944 (Wikipedia, 34th Armoured Brigade). Event definition: Operation Rebound, part of Operation Pheasant, begins on 20 October with a barrage by the 49th Division artillery; the 56th Infantry Brigade and the 9th Royal Tank Regiment seize Stapelheide as a start line for Clarkeforce, a column round the brigade, which goes through at 4 p.m.; on 22 October the advance continues towards Esschen (Wikipedia). Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, 34th Armoured Brigade (page 34th Tank Brigade): "Operation Rebound (part of the larger Operation Pheasant) began on 20 October"; "On 22 October, the advance continued towards Esschen". Location support: Wikipedia names Stapelheide and the advance towards Esschen (Essen). Commander: Brig. W. S. Clarke, commander from June 1943 (Wikipedia, 34th Armoured Brigade).

notes: Event date: 6 November 1944, the day Willemstad was liberated (Wikipedia, 34th Armoured Brigade). Event definition: After Clarkeforce is disbanded, the 49th Division advances to its final objective, Willemstad on the Hollands Diep, in a conventional infantry advance (Operation Humid) supported by the brigade in its infantry-tank role; Willemstad is liberated on 6 November after the German garrison withdraws across the Maas (Wikipedia). Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, 34th Armoured Brigade (page 34th Tank Brigade): "supported by the 34th Tank Brigade in its more familiar infantry tank role"; "Willemstad was liberated on 6 November after the German garrison withdrew across the Maas".
